name: Cocoa Fudge Brownies (Baker by Nature)
description: Faithful import of Baker by Nature's 'The Best Cocoa Fudge Brownies' - the full-sugar, full-butter indulgent reference brownie, no substitutions. Crackly-top technique: a third of the sugar melts into the hot butter + oil, then the warm fat streams slowly into well-whisked eggs; that dissolved sugar is what bakes the shiny cracked top. Cocoa-only chocolate flavor (plus espresso powder), semi-sweet chips folded in whole. 9x9 pan, cut 16. This is the indulgent yardstick the lean bakes get judged against - macros are what they are (~170g butter, 265g sugar per pan).

steps.instructionText: Sift together the flour, baking powder, salt, cocoa powder, and espresso powder. Set aside. Line a 9x9-inch pan with parchment and lightly grease; preheat the oven to 350F.
In a saucepan combine the butter, oil, and 65g (1/3 cup) of the sugar. Heat over medium, stirring frequently, just until the butter melts. Remove from heat.
In a large bowl whisk the eggs, egg yolk, vanilla, and the remaining 200g (1 cup) sugar until well combined.
Slowly pour the warm butter mixture into the egg mixture, adding gradually and whisking constantly until fully combined.

Add the dry ingredients and chocolate chips; fold with a spatula until JUST combined - stop while you still see the slightest trace of dry. Do not over mix. Scrape into the prepared pan and smooth the top.
Bake at 350F for 28-30 min, until the edges are firm and the top is shiny and slightly cracked. Pull at 27 min for gooey; 30-32 min for more structure. Cool completely on a rack before slicing 16.

notes.text: The crackly top is engineered in two moves: melting part of the sugar into the hot butter/oil, then streaming that warm fat slowly into thoroughly-whisked eggs. Dissolved sugar migrating to the surface is what bakes shiny and cracked - skip the saucepan step and you get a matte top.
Stop folding when you still see the slightest trace of dry ingredients. Overmixing after the flour goes in toughens the crumb and knocks out the fudge.
Doneness is a dial, not a point: 27 min = gooey, 28-30 = fudgy (edges firm, top shiny/cracked), 30-32 = sliceable structure. Cool COMPLETELY before cutting - warm brownies read underbaked.
